tasks.title: Migrate divergent worktree planners through a lossless reviewed binding
tasks.description:
Outcome: Previewed, lossless migration from legacy planner copies to a descriptor-bound SQLite project.

Current implementation: Tracked .planner copies can diverge. Legacy docs/custom skills and active process ownership require explicit treatment; old migration waited on advanced target integration unnecessarily.

Implementation responsibility:
- Inventory legacy copies and live writers; create immutable backups with source schema/worktree/branch/revision provenance before proposing activation.
- Stage and reconcile entities, counters, requirements, single-owner decisions, handoffs/archives, checkpoints and all linked documents/assets. Import custom skills/guidance into DB content and map filesystem references to document identities.
- Use common identity/baselines where available; preserve conflicting fields and unknown provenance. Never use latest mtime, whole-file wins or fabricated old execution/merge evidence.
- Validate schema, parent containment, references, cycles and document completeness. Activate transactionally and write the descriptor only after durable success; journal partial migration/descriptor publication for recovery.
- Make old sources explicit read-only backups; incompatible old writers must not create competing authority. Exclude stale locks/PIDs/credentials and do not restore live ownership.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Divergent two-worktree imports preserve all knowledge or expose exact conflicts before activation.
- Crashes at staging/commit/descriptor boundaries retain one recoverable authority and original backup.
- Initial migration is usable after T490, without waiting for T492; later execution schemas retain explicit unknown legacy provenance.
- Tests use isolated temporary projects; real migration/tracking changes need their implementation-time authorization.

tasks.title: Add recoverable planner history, backup and portable export/restore
tasks.description:
Outcome: Independent backup, conflict-aware snapshot export/import and descriptor-based restore.

Current implementation: Current Markdown export is not a complete portable backup. Files in git-common-dir/HOME are not copied by ordinary source clone/push, and a lost acknowledgement can hide a successful publication.

Implementation responsibility:
- Use consistent SQLite backups and read snapshot revision from the snapshot itself. Configure retention, independent destinations and distinct local-backup/remote-publication status.
- Export versioned logical JSON plus manifest/project/revision/baseline/hashes and all required documents/source-evidence assets; omit credentials, active ownership, PIDs, caches and inherited read authorization.
- Implement explicit UI/tool snapshot publication using a private bare Git transport and normal authenticated commit/push. Fetch/import must leave source checkout/index/branch untouched; ordinary planner updates do not auto-publish.
- Compare both local baseline and fetched remote tip. Stage common-baseline reconciliation for divergent computers, retaining same-field/delete-edit/lifecycle conflicts and validating the resulting graph before activation.
- Recheck the local revision at import activation, preserve backup and support interruption/status lookup. Descriptor-only clones and missing-HOME cases recover up to the last complete available snapshot, never unpublished data.
- Document limits: local DB claims are not team-wide ownership, snapshots are not a network authority, and restoring planner knowledge does not revert source code.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Round-trip restore preserves IDs, decisions, handoffs and portable evidence without old absolute paths or resurrected sessions.
- Remote divergence cannot silently overwrite another snapshot; retry after unknown publication outcome does not duplicate it.
- No force push, pull into the live DB, required personal hook, operational mirror or shared-drive SQLite.
- Backup/restore is available for the first usable migrated DB release and uses isolated crash/conflict fixtures.
